name: Saint Thomas the Apostle
history: One of the Twelve, called Didymus, the Twin. He would not believe the others had seen the risen Lord until he could touch His wounds, and when Christ came again he made the clearest confession of faith in the Gospels: ‘My Lord and my God.’ Ancient tradition holds that he carried the Gospel to India and was martyred there.
life: Saint John’s Gospel gives Thomas a voice of his own. When Jesus resolved to go back to Judaea, where His enemies waited, it was Thomas who said, ‘Let us also go, that we may die with Him.’ At the Last Supper he asked, ‘Lord, we do not know where You are going; how can we know the way?’, and drew the answer, ‘I am the way, the truth and the life.’ Absent when the risen Christ first appeared, he refused to believe without touching the wounds. Eight days later Christ invited him to do so, and he cried out, ‘My Lord and my God.’ Christ blessed those who have not seen and yet believe. The Christians of Kerala in southern India, who call themselves Saint Thomas Christians, trace their faith to him, and tradition places his martyrdom by a spear near Chennai. His relics were later honoured at Edessa and at Ortona in Italy.
prayerTo: Saint Thomas, you were brave enough to go with Christ to death and honest enough to say you could not believe. Pray for all who doubt, and for the Christians of India. When my faith is weak, lead me to the wounds of Christ, so that I too may say, ‘My Lord and my God.’ Amen.
penance: At the elevation at Mass, or before the tabernacle, say quietly, ‘My Lord and my God.’ Pray for someone you know who struggles to believe.
meditation: Christ did not scold Thomas for his doubt; He showed him His wounds. What doubt could you bring honestly to Him today?
